# Range Slider

> A two-thumb slider for picking a range, with a thumb at each end that can meet but not pass the other.

`<slab-range-slider>` · Form · built on `<input type=range>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/range-slider/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/range-slider.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-range-slider
  label="Price"
  name="price"
  min="0"
  max="500"
  start-value="100"
  end-value="300"
></slab-range-slider>
```

Each thumb is named by `label` and then its own label, "Minimum" and "Maximum" unless you set `start-label` and `end-label`, so a screenreader reads "Price Minimum". The form gets two entries under `name`, the start and then the end. Give the track a size, since the thumbs and the range between them are placed along it.

Inside each thumb is a visually hidden range input. It's what has focus and what a screenreader reads, which lets screenreaders on phones adjust a thumb with a swipe up or down. Since the thumb itself isn't focused, it can't match `:focus-visible`. Style its focus ring through `::part(focus-visible)`, which the thumb has while its input's focus is visible.

Screenreaders read each thumb's value as a bare number. When it means more than that, set `formatValue` to a function of the value, such as `` (value) => `$${value}` ``, and they'll read what it returns instead.

Its range is always in bounds, so it's never invalid on its own. For a rule of your own, such as a minimum width, call `setCustomValidity()` with a message. It shows in `::part(validity-message)`, and the host matches `:state(error)`, once validity is reported, as on [Text Field](text-field.md): when focus leaves the slider, when its form is submitted, or on `reportValidity()`.

`stepUp()` and `stepDown()` step a thumb by `step` from code, as a range input's do, such as for buttons beside the slider. Pass "start" or "end" after the count to pick the thumb, as in `stepUp(1, 'end')`. Without one, they step the thumb that has focus, or the start thumb when neither does. A thumb is kept to `min` or `max` and to the other thumb, and neither method dispatches "input" or "change".

## Keyboard

| Key                   | What it does                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left, Down, Right, Up | Steps the focused thumb down or up by `step`. Left and Right move it the way the arrow points. |
| Page Up, Page Down    | Steps it by a tenth of the range.                                                              |
| Home, End             | Moves it as far as it can go: to `min` or `max`, or to the other thumb.                        |

## Elements

### `<slab-range-slider>`

Import `slab-elements/range-slider.js` to register it.

A two-thumb slider with no visual styles, for picking a range, such as a price from one amount to another. It follows the APG multi-thumb slider pattern: each thumb is a `[role=slider]`, and each one's minimum or maximum is the other thumb, so the two can meet but not pass each other.

A range input has only one thumb, so the thumbs are elements of their own rather than two range inputs on top of each other, which can't report each other as their bounds and fight over the pointer where they overlap. Inside each is a visually hidden range input, which is what's focused and what a screenreader reads. A range input is what screenreaders on phones know how to adjust, with a swipe up or down, which they can't do to a `[role=slider]`.

`start-value` and `end-value` are the range, and they're always between `min` and `max`, on a `step` from `min`, and in order. Unset, they're `min` and `max`, so the whole range is picked. Like a native input's `value`, their attributes are the defaults and their properties the current values.

The group is named by `label`, and each thumb by it and its own label, so a screenreader reads "Price Minimum" and "Price Maximum". The arrow keys move a thumb by `step`, Page Up and Page Down by a tenth of the range, and Home and End as far as it can go. Drag a thumb, or press the track to bring the nearer thumb there.

Screenreaders read each thumb's value as a number. Set `formatValue` to a function of it that says what it means, such as "$40", which becomes each input's `aria-valuetext`.

Its range is always in bounds, so it's never invalid on its own. For a rule of your own, such as a minimum width, call `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`. The validity message shows in its description, as on Text Field, once validity is reported: when focus leaves it, its form is submitted, or `reportValidity()` is called.

Placing the thumbs and the range between them along the track is what a slider does, so that's functional and done here: each thumb is centered on its value, and the range spans from one to the other. Give the track a size, and style the rest through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(dragging)` and `:state(error)`. Focus is on the input inside a thumb, so a thumb whose input has visible focus has a `focus-visible` part for a focus ring.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |             | Names the group. Each thumb is named by it and its own label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `disabled`         | `boolean` | `false`     | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `end-label`        | `string`  |             | Names the end thumb, after `label`. "Maximum" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `end-value`        | `number`  | `undefined` | Like a native input's `value`, the attribute is the default and the property is the current value. Between `start-value` and `max`, on a step. `max` when unset.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false`     | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `max`              | `number`  | `100`       | The highest either end can be.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `min`              | `number`  | `0`         | The lowest either end can be.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `name`             | `string`  | `''`        | Submitted twice, with the start value and then the end value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `start-label`      | `string`  |             | Names the start thumb, after `label`. "Minimum" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `start-value`      | `number`  | `undefined` | Like a native input's `value`, the attribute is the default and the property is the current value. Between `min` and `end-value`, on a step. `min` when unset.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `step`             | `number`  | `1`         | How far apart the values either end can take are, as a native range input's `step`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `custom-validity`  | `string`  |             | Makes it invalid with this message, as `setCustomValidity()` does, and shows the message at once rather than once validity is reported, for an error the page already knows about, such as one from a server. Removing it, or setting it to an empty string, makes it valid again, unless something else makes it invalid. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formatValue`                   | `(value: number) => string \| undefined` | What screenreaders read for each thumb's value, such as "$40" rather than "40". The value itself when unset.                                                                                                                      |
| `defaultEndValue`               | `number \| undefined`                    | The end value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `end-value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is its `value` attribute, so setting it sets the attribute, and `endValue` with it.       |
| `defaultStartValue`             | `number \| undefined`                    | The start value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `start-value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is its `value` attribute, so setting it sets the attribute, and `startValue` with it. |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`                | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `labels` (read-only)            | `NodeList`                               | The `<label>` elements associated with it, as a native control's `labels`: each `<label for>` that names its `id`, and a `<label>` around it.                                                                                     |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                                 | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`. Empty while it's valid.                                                                                             |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`                          | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                                | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                                                                 |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `stepDown(count?: number, thumb?: 'start' \| 'end'): void`        | Steps a thumb down by `step` times `count`, as a native range input's `stepDown()` does, as far as `min` or the start thumb. `thumb` is "start" or "end". Left out, it's the thumb that has focus, or the start thumb when neither does. Like a native input's, it dispatches no events. |
| `stepUp(count?: number, thumb?: 'start' \| 'end'): void`          | Steps a thumb up by `step` times `count`, as a native range input's `stepUp()` does, as far as `max` or the end thumb. `thumb` is "start" or "end". Left out, it's the thumb that has focus, or the start thumb when neither does. Like a native input's, it dispatches no events.       |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.               |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.             |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown. |

#### Slots

| Name               | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `validity-message` | `Element \| string` | Shown in place of the validity message's text while it's invalid and the message shows, for wording of your own, a translation, or a link. It's part of its accessible description, and `validationMessage` stays the browser's or `setCustomValidity()`'s. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`        | The label, the track and the description                        |
| `description`      | Text about the slider, and its validity message when it has one |
| `end`              | The end thumb                                                   |
| `focus-visible`    | The thumb whose input has visible focus                         |
| `label`            | The label                                                       |
| `range`            | The part of the track between the thumbs                        |
| `start`            | The start thumb                                                 |
| `track`            | The thumbs and the range between them                           |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid       |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(dragging)` | While the user drags a thumb.                                                                                             |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
